answer: A desert atlas office gives each agent one sheet covering a single oasis, and the sheet earns standing only by recording that oasis lotus pond bloom by bloom. Each season the keeper walks the ground, counts open blooms, and files a pond edge sketch. Two neighboring keepers walk the same ground that week and file their own counts; the sheet stays valid only when two counts match within five blooms, or it goes dark for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand walked surveys and a thousand matching neighbor counts, so copying one sheet buys nothing.
